caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The plot displays training loss curves over iterations for five different models: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations (SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128)). The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000 with tick marks at intervals of 20,000, labeled as "#Iteration". The y-axis represents the loss, scaled linearly from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. All curves begin at a loss value exceeding 3.4 at iteration 0 and decrease rapidly within the first 20,000 iterations. The Vanilla model, shown as a purple line with circular markers, starts at a loss of approximately 3.4 and converges to a final loss of about 2.45 by iteration 140,000. The StrmLLM (n=64) model, represented by a blue line with circular markers, begins at a loss of approximately 3.4 and converges to a loss of about 2.60. The SepLLM (n=64) model, shown in orange with circular markers, starts at approximately 3.4 and converges to a loss of around 2.51. The SepLLM (n=64, H) model, depicted in green with circular markers, begins at approximately 3.4 and converges to a loss of about 2.52. The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) model, shown in red with circular markers, starts at approximately 3.4 and converges to a loss of around 2.49. The SepLLM (n=128) model, represented by a dark blue line with circular markers, begins at approximately 3.4 and converges to a loss of about 2.55. After the initial rapid decline, all curves exhibit a slower rate of convergence, with the loss values stabilizing near their final values by iteration 140,000.
